subject: Post-call: Meridian Labs — tech scope & prompt safety plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Meridian Labs — tech scope & prompt safety plan

Hi Evan / Claire,

Thanks again for the time today — nice to meet the Meridian product and infra teams. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan heading into a technical deep-dive: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use case: customer support assistant + knowledge retrieval over internal docs (long context, frequent updates).
- Latency SLO: 200–300ms 95p for short chat; bursty embedding/semantic search during overnight jobs.
- Security: SSO (Okta), strict data residency (US), KMS for keys, SOC2 evidence requested.
- Important features: structured tool-calling for open URL lookups, reranker for results, prompt versioning and red-team process.

Proposed architecture highlights (high-level)
1) SDK + auth: use Redwood JS/Go SDK for client calls; short-lived tokens via Okta -> Redwood token exchange. We can demo both token-exchange and service-account KMS encrypted key paths.
2) Routing: primary routing to hosted Redwood model (low-latency), fallback to dedicated pool for larger batches/embeddings. Policy per-route.
3) Embeddings + rerank: periodic bulk embeddings to your S3 (or use Redwood-managed storage), lightweight reranker housed in the same inference runtime to avoid cross-region hop.
4) Structured output / tool calling: use Redwood structured response schema to return JSON for tool calls (example in attachments).
5) Prompt governance: store system prompts in versioned config (Git-backed), automated A/B flagging, and injection mitigation via input sanitization + contextual allow-listing.

Immediate next steps
- Schedule 60–90m technical deep-dive with your infra & security (suggest Weds/Thurs next week) — decision makers: Evan, Claire, and your infra lead.
- I’ll share a short SDK snippet + structured-output example and a basic threat model doc for prompt injection scenarios.
- Please send over the Okta metadata (metadata URL / issuer), KMS preference, and any sample doc indexes you want us to test embeddings on.

Attachments: meridian-ma-arch.pdf (high-level arch), redwood-sdk-sample.md (quickstart + snippets), prompt-versioning-guidelines.docx (governance outline)

Thanks — I’ll coordinate times after you confirm availability.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed answers + sample snippets

Evan / Claire — quick follow-up with concrete answers and a few inline snippets.

Embeddings storage: yes — Redwood supports pointing to customer-managed vector stores (S3 + Dynamo + VPC endpoints). We also offer managed vector cycles if you prefer. For your flow I recommend: bulk embed -> store vectors in your S3 + Dynamo table -> Redwood SDK calls can return nearest-neighbors with metadata and pass IDs to your reranker.

Reranker options: two patterns we see work well:
- Redwood-first: Redwood produces candidate set + scores, then call your internal reranker as a final scoring pass (keep your business rules).
- Hybrid: Redwood returns dense vector candidates and a light-weight model for final local scoring (less network hops).
Recommendation: start with Redwood-first to simplify rollout, then migrate heavy logic to your Python reranker if you need fine-grained business rules.

Auth flows (short):
- Okta -> Redwood token exchange (recommended for user-context calls)
- Service account w/ KMS (recommended for server-side batch jobs)

Routing policy (example):
- Chat routes: low-latency hosted (gpt-like open model), 95p < 300ms target
- Batch/embed routes: dedicated pool or self-managed batch windows to control cost

Structured output (tool calling) example (JSON schema):
{"response_type":"tool_call","tool":"kb_lookup","args":{"document_id":"doc_123","cursor":42}}

SDK snippet (JS) — short example calling structured output and handling tool-calls:
```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
const res = await client.generate({
  model: 'redwood-chat-v1',
  input: userPrompt,
  structuredOutput: true
});
if (res.output[0].response_type === 'tool_call') {
  // call local service with args
  await callKb(res.output[0].args.document_id);
}
```

Prompt governance highlights:
- Store system prompts in versioned Git file (prompt_v1, prompt_v2) — track changes + rollbacks.
- Prompt injection mitigations: canonicalize and escape user content, use explicit task-oriented system prompts, and instrument runtime checks that drop or neutralize suspicious tokens.
- Red-team: we recommend a monthly red-team run using both auto-generated adversarial inputs and human review; store failing prompts as test cases in the eval harness.

Attachments: sdk-snippets.zip contains a runnable example for Okta token exchange + structured-output handler.

Ava — looping you in to confirm if we should include Tessa (security) in the deep-dive and to propose the exact agenda.

Best,
Ben
